mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the prediction is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the prior month
regime_hint: tightening cycle after a period of easing
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during confirmed tightening phases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer pay growth (HOUST) predict negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns as weak wage growth dampens corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while HOUST decreases in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) when the interaction signal is present.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% above its prior month's value coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals resilient demand for capital goods.
failure_condition: No significant return (p > 0.05) in 20-day window despite INDPRO exceeding +2% in the month prior.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer confidence (implied via HOUST) for two consecutive months predicts a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals supply-side contraction.
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is positive and robust across multiple such double-consecutive declines.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.5% for three consecutive months during a monetary easing regime, the S&P 500 is expected to deliver a positive 60-day forward return as market anticipates sustained hiring.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.5% for 3 consecutive months and FEDFUNDS < 2% in the same window
failure_condition: No significant positive 60-day return (p > 0.05) when trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in monthly pay growth (HOUST) above 2% followed by a decline in job openings (implied via PAYEMS) predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as wage inflation without job growth risks wage-price imbalance.
candidate_trigger: HOUST crosses above 2% while PAYEMS decreases in the same month
regime_hint: wage acceleration without labor market expansion
failure_condition: 20-day return is positive and significant when the interaction occurs.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in retail sales (implied via CPIAUCSL > 0.2% YoY increase after flat or negative prior month) predicts a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals demand recovery.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by >0.2% in month after ≤0% prior month
failure_condition: 5-day return is not positive or not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in industrial production (INDPRO) of at least 3% indicate a supply shock, predicting a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates earnings compression.
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is positive or not significantly different from zero during such sequences.
